chunks: From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Al-Hasan al-Zayyat, who said:
I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) having lightened his beard.

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, referring to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him)
key_terms.خَفَّفَ: He lightened/trimmed (implying reducing fullness or length without shaving)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Abu Ja'far do with his beard according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This brief narration from al-Kafi records Imam al-Baqir’s (AS) personal grooming practice of trimming or 'lightening' his beard, providing a crucial Prophetic precedent for the Shia juristic debate on whether the beard must be kept fully thick or if trimming is permissible. It underscores the distinction between the Sunnah of the Imams and the later rigidifications in fiqh, highlighting the Imam's adherence to a balanced, natural appearance rather than an exaggerated fullness.

en.hubeali: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Al Hassan Al Zayyat who said,
‘I saw Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having lightened his<sup>asws</sup> beard’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan from al-Hassan al-Zayyat who has said the following: “
I once saw abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, had made his beard lighter.’”
